scope: One fresh controlled Gmail alias completed rendered email registration, mailbox verification, credential sign-in and workbench navigation in a Chrome extension-controlled browser on current private Version 17. After a stable no-error workbench read state, two bounded non-sensitive early-riser habit attempts showed the client network/login guidance without a visible check-in. The test account was then requested for deletion, confirmed for deletion, refreshed, and no longer rendered its profile. No email address, password, verification link, recovery token, browser cookie, storage value, mailbox body, or business record was retained.

interpretation.proven: The current private Version 17 completed a real rendered email registration, verification, credential login, verified-session account read and account-deletion lifecycle in the Chrome extension-controlled surface. The workbench showed a stable no-error read state before the second bounded habit attempt, but both non-sensitive habit POST attempts ended in the client fetch-exception guidance without visible record creation. The successful account deletion POST means this observation is not evidence that the newly verified account could not execute every authenticated mutation.
not_proven: A normal end-user browser outside the agent-controlled Chrome extension completed or failed a workbench mutation
A Worker, D1, R2, or Better Auth production defect
Successful ordinary-browser habit creation, history readback, or physical second-device synchronization
A current Version 17 email provider negative-delivery result
interpretation.decision: Do not weaken authentication, duplicate or rename workbench APIs, relax same-origin protections, or alter the frozen visual baseline merely to bypass this agent-controlled browser transport boundary. The still-required ordinary-browser replay must use a browser surface outside this guard.
